title: How to Change Claude's Tone & Voice (iOS, Android & Web)
description: Change Claude's spoken Voice Mode on iOS/Android vs written tone in Profile Preferences, Projects, Skills, and Claude Code /output-style. 6 presets.
h1: How to change Claude's tone and voice on iOS, Android, and web.
dek: Spoken audio voices live in mobile Voice Mode settings; written personality lives in Profile Preferences, Projects, Skills, and /output-style.
lede: When someone searches "how to change Claude's voice or tone," they are looking for one of two different menus: either switching the spoken audio voice in Claude's mobile Voice Mode, or changing how Claude writes and reasons across web and mobile chats. Anthropic separates those two controls cleanly—and knowing which menu owns which layer saves five minutes of hunting through Settings.
answer: To change Claude's spoken audio voice on iOS or Android, open Voice Mode (the waveform icon) or tap your initials → Settings → Voice and choose from the available spoken voices. To change Claude's written tone across web and mobile, tap your initials → Settings → Profile (or General) → 'What personal preferences should Claude consider in responses?' and paste 6–10 concrete rules.

sections.h2: Spoken Voice Mode vs. Written Tone: exact tap paths.
sections.html:
What you want to changeSurfaceExact menu path
Spoken audio voice (pitch/timbre in Voice Mode)Claude iOS & Android appsTap the Voice Mode waveform icon in the composer (or Initials → Settings → Voice) → pick your preferred voice option.
Account-wide written tone (every new chat)claude.ai web, macOS/Windows, iOS & AndroidTap Initials → Settings → Profile (or General) → What personal preferences should Claude consider in responses?
One workspace's written toneClaude ProjectsOpen the Project → Project instructions (overrides conflicting Profile lines inside that Project).
Task-triggered writing formatsClaude Skills (replacing retired Styles)Package repeatable templates as Skills (read the Styles → Skills migration guide).
Terminal coding toneClaude Code CLIRun /output-style or edit ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (Claude Code guide).

Because Profile Personal Preferences sync on your Anthropic account, pasting a written tone block once on claude.ai updates how Claude phrases spoken replies on iOS and Android too—long wind-ups and bulleted lists sound awkward out loud, so concise prose rules make mobile Voice Mode dramatically better.

sections.h2: Six copy-paste written tone presets (including a Voice-Mode friendly preset).
sections.html:
1. Direct peer (everyday default)

- Answer in the first sentence with no throat-clearing preamble. - Default to clear prose; use bullet lists only for 3+ parallel items or step-by-step commands. - Push back directly when my plan has a flaw and explain the concrete tradeoff. - Ask at most one clarifying question only when missing context changes the answer. - Flag material uncertainty explicitly rather than guessing.

2. Mobile & Voice Mode friendly (clean spoken cadence)

- Keep default answers to 2–4 natural sentences unless I ask you to go deeper. - Avoid markdown tables, nested bullets, and raw URLs unless I ask for written reference output. - Lead with the takeaway, then stop and let me steer what to unpack next.

3. Skeptical reviewer (anti-sycophancy)

- Never open with praise ('Great idea!', 'You're right to think about...'). - Identify the weakest assumption or highest-risk failure mode first. - Distinguish verified facts from inference and propose a falsifiable check.

4. Calm step-by-step coach

- Break multi-part problems into manageable sequential steps and confirm scope before expanding. - Keep tone steady, plain, and practical—skip alarmist warnings and ungrounded reassurance.

5. Executive brief

- Open with a 1-sentence recommendation, followed by key tradeoffs, cost/risk, and next action. - Use tables only when comparing 3+ options across identical criteria.

6. Deep technical mechanisms

- Assume senior engineering familiarity; skip introductory definitions of standard tools. - Explain the underlying mechanism and invariant before showing a patch or command.

sections.h2: What measured pilot data shows when you tune Claude.
sections.html: In our 60-reply controlled pilot (20 real tasks across default Claude, plain behavioral rules, and conversational partner framing), adding explicit behavioral rules raised answer-first openings from 14/20 to 19/20, reduced average hedges per reply from 0.35 to 0.05, and lowered end-of-message follow-up questions from 0.90 to 0.25. Validate your chosen block on two real tasks from last week using our Instruction Test Bench.

faq.q: How do I change Claude's voice on the iPhone or Android app?
faq.a: To switch the spoken voice timbre in Voice Mode, tap the waveform icon in the mobile composer or open your initials → Settings → Voice. To change Claude's phrasing, brevity, and directness, open Settings → Profile and paste rules into Personal Preferences.

faq.q: Where did Claude's 'Styles' selector (Concise, Formal, Explanatory) go?
faq.a: Anthropic retired standalone Styles in favor of account-wide Personal Preferences for your baseline voice and reusable Skills/Projects for task-specific formats.

faq.q: Do my Claude web Personal Preferences apply to the mobile app and Voice Mode?
faq.a: Yes. Personal Preferences are stored on your Anthropic account and shape responses across claude.ai web, desktop apps, and mobile chats—which is why keeping default answers concise improves Voice Mode listening.

faq.q: How do I change Claude's tone inside Claude Code in the terminal?
faq.a: Claude Code does not read claude.ai web Personal Preferences. Put coding communication rules in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or install a style file in ~/.claude/output-styles/ and select it via /output-style.
